reason: The if/else-if chain in wpa_ft_set_key_mgmt only handles WPA_KEY_MGMT_FT_IEEE8021X(_SHA384)/FT_PSK/FT_FILS_SHA256/FT_FILS_SHA384, but defs.h also defines WPA_KEY_MGMT_FT_SAE and WPA_KEY_MGMT_FT_SAE_EXT_KEY as valid FT AKMs; if key_mgmt (already validated non-zero at line 3024) is one of those unhandled bits, sm->wpa_key_mgmt is silently left unset while the function still returns 0 (success), a real state-inconsistency bug for FT-SAE.

The dispatch chain over dbus dictionary keys (Role/Type/Bssid/Pin/P2PDeviceAddress) falls through to unconditional code right after the chain (lines 204-206) that logs 'unknown key', builds a DBus error reply, and returns -1, so the unmatched-key case is fully handled -- just not via a final else.

In wpa_supplicant_event_global, the if/else-if only special-cases finding wpa_s via ifindex vs. handling EVENT_INTERFACE_ADDED under CONFIG_MATCH_IFACE; when neither branch matches, control falls through to the unconditional 'if (wpa_s) wpa_supplicant_event(...)' below, which is the intended default behavior (do nothing further if no interface was resolved), not an unhandled case.

The imsi-selection chain (cred->imsi / PCSC_FUNCS / CONFIG_EAP_PROXY) leaves imsi as NULL if none of the branches match, but the very next code (line 2311-2312) already guards on 'imsi &&' before using it, so the unhandled case is deliberately treated as 'no IMSI available' and safely skipped, not a silent bug.
